outcomes.text: Personal responsibility: Accepts responsibility for improving one’s own levels of physical activity and fitness.
Personal responsibility: Uses effective self-monitoring skills to incorporate opportunities for physical activity in and outside of school.
Accepting feedback: Provides encouragement and feedback to peers without prompting from the teacher.
Working with others: Responds appropriately to participants’ ethical and unethical behavior during physical activity by using rules and guidelines for resolving conflicts.

subtopics.title: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others.: (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Working with others: Cooperates with multiple classmates on problem-solving initiatives, including adventure activities, large-group initiatives, and game-play.
Rules and etiquette: Applies rules and etiquette by acting as an official for modified physical activities and games and creating dance routines within a given set of parameters.
Safety: Independently uses physical activity and fitness equipment appropriately, and identifies specific safety concerns associated with the activity.

units.title: Recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction.:

topics.title: Recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction.:

subtopics.title: Recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction.:

outcomes.text: Health: Identifies the 5 components of health-related fitness (muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility, cardiorespiratory endurance, and body composition) and explains the connections between fitness and overall physical and mental health.
Health: Analyzes the empowering consequences of being physically active.
Challenge: Develops a plan of action and makes appropriate decisions based on that plan when faced with an individual challenge.
Self-expression and enjoyment: Discusses how enjoyment could be increased in self-selected physical activities.
Self-expression and enjoyment: Identifies and participates in an enjoyable activity that prompts individual selfexpression.
Social interaction: Demonstrates respect for self by asking for help and helping others in various physical activities.

units.title: Standard 1: Demonstrates competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns

outcomes.text: Level 1 :Demonstrates competency and/or refines activity-specific movement skills in 2 or more lifetime activities (outdoor pursuits, individual performance activities, aquatics, net/wall games, or target games).
Level 2: Refines activity-specific movement skills in 1 or more lifetime activities (outdoor pursuits, individual-performance activities, aquatics, net/wall games, or target games).
Level 1: Demonstrates competency in dance forms used in cultural and social occasions (e.g. weddings, parties) or demonstrates competency in 1 form of dance (e.g. ballet, modern, hip hop, tap).
Level 2: Demonstrates competency in a form of dance by choreographing a dance or by giving a performance.
Level 1: Demonstrates competency in 1 or more specialized skills in health related fitness activities
Level 2: Demonstrates competency in 2 or more specialized skills in health related fitness activities.

units.title: Standard 2: Applies knowledge of concepts, principals, strategies and tactics related to movement and performance

subtopics.title: Movement concepts, principles and knowledge: (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Level 1: Applies the terminology associated with exercise and participation in selected individual-performance activities, dance, net/wall games, target games, aquatics, and/or outdoor pursuits appropriately
Level 2: Identifies and discusses the historical and cultural roles of games, sports, and dance in a society.
Level 1: Uses movement concepts and principles (e.g. force, motion, rotation) to analyze and improve performance of self and/or others in a selected skill.
Level 2: Describes the speed/accuracy trade-off in throwing and striking skills.

subtopics.title: Movement concepts, principles and knowledge: (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Level 1: Creates a practice plan to improve performance for a self-selected skill
Level 2: Identifies the stages of learning a motor skill.
Level 1: Identifies examples of social and technical dance forms.
Level 2: Compares similarities and difference in various dance forms. (S2.4.L2

units.title: Standard 3: Demonstrates the knowledge and skills to achieve a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness

outcomes.text: Level 1:Discusses the benefits of a physical activity active lifestyle as it relates to college or career productivity.
Level 2: Investigates the relationships among physical activity, nutrition, and body composition.
Level 1: Evaluates the validity of claims made by commercial products and programs pertaining to fitness and a healthy, active lifestyle.
Level 2: Analyzes and applies technology and social media as tools for supporting a healthy, active lifestyle.
Level 1: Identifies issues associated with exercising in heat, humidity, and cold.
Level 2: Applies rates of perceived exertion and pacing.
Level 1: Evaluates – according to their benefits, social support network, and participation requirements – activities that can be pursued in the local environment. S3.4.L1
Level 2: If the outcome was not achieved in Level 1, it should be a focus in Level 2.
Level 1: Evaluates risks and safety factors that might affect physical activity preferences throughout the life cycle. S3.5.L1
Level 2: Analyzes the impact of life choices, economics, motivation, and accessibility on exercise adherence and participation in physical activity in college or career settings. S3.5.L2
Level 1: Participates several times a week in a self-selected lifetime activity, dance or fitness activity outside of the school day.S3.6.L1
Level 2: Creates a plan, trains for, and participates in a community event with a focus on physical activity (e.g. 5K, triathlon, tournament, dance performance, cycling event). S3.6.L2
Level 1: Demonstrates appropriate technique in resistance-training machines and free-weights. S3.7.L1
Level 2: Designs and implements a strength and conditioning program that develops balance in opposing muscle groups (agonist-antagonist) and supports a healthy, active lifestyle. S3.7.L2
Level 1: Relates physiological responses to individual levels of fitness and nutritional balance. S3.8.L1
Level 2: Identifies the different energy systems used in a selected physical activity (e.g. adenosine triphosphate and phosphocreatine, anaerobic glycolysis, aerobic). S3.8.L2

Level 1: Identifies types of strength exercises (isometric, concentric, eccentric) and stretching exercises (static, proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF), dynamic) for personal fitness development (e.g. strength, endurance, range of motion). S3.9.L1
Level 2: Identifies the structure of skeletal muscle and fiber types as they relate to muscle development. S3.9.L1
Level 1: Calculates target heart rate and applies that information to personal fitness plan. S3.10.L1
Level 2: Adjusts pacing to keep heart rate in the target zone, using available technology (e.g. pedometer, heart rate monitor), to self-monitor aerobic intensity. S3.10.L2
Level 1: Creates and implements a behavior-modification plan that enhances a healthy, active lifestyle in college or career settings. S3.11.L1

Level 2: Develops and maintains a fitness portfolio (e.g. assessment scores, goals for improvement, plan of activities for improvement, log of activities being done to reach goals, timeline for improvement). S3.11.L2
Level 1: Designs a fitness program, including all components of health-related fitness, for a college student and an employee in the learner’s chosen field of work.
Level 2: Analyzes the components of skill-related fitness in relation to life and career goals and designs an appropriate fitness program for those goals. S3.12.L2
Level 1: Designs and implements a nutrition plan to maintain an appropriate energy balance for a healthy, active lifestyle. S3.13.L1
Level 2: Creates a snack plan for before, during, and after exercise that addresses nutrition needs for each phase. S3.13.L2
Level 1: Identifies stress-management strategies (e.g. mental imagery, relaxation techniques, deep breathing, aerobic exercise, and meditation) to reduce stress. S3.14.L1
Level 2: Applies stress-management strategies (e.g. mental imagery, relaxation techniques, deep breathing, aerobic exercise, and meditation) to reduce stress. S3.14.L2

units.title: Standard 4: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others

outcomes.text: Level 1: Employs effective self-management skills to analyze barriers and modify physical activity patterns appropriately as needed. S4.1.L1
Level 2: Accepts differences between personal characteristics and the idealized body images and elite performance levels portrayed in various media. S4.1.L2
Level 1: Exhibits proper etiquette, respect for others, and teamwork while engaging in physical activity and/or social dance. S4.2.L1
Level 2: Examines moral and ethical conduct in specific competitive situations (e.g. intentional fouls, performance-enhancing substances, gambling, current events in sport). S4.2.L2
Level 1: Uses communication skills and strategies that promote team or group dynamics. S4.3.L1
Level 2: Assumes a leadership role (e.g. task or group leader, referee, coach) in a physical activity setting. S4.3.L2
Level 1: Solves problems and thinks critically in physical activity or dance settings, both as an individual and in groups. S4.4.L1
Level 2: Accepts others’ ideas, cultural diversity, and body types by engaging in cooperative and collaborative movement projects. S4.4.L2

Level 1: Applies best practices for participating safely in physical activity, exercise and dance (e.g. injury prevention, proper alignment, hydration, use of equipment, implementation of rules, sun protection).
Level 2: If the outcome was not achieved in Level 1, it should be a focus in Level 2. S4.5.L2

units.title: Standard 5: Recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or social interaction

outcomes.text: Level 1: Analyzes the health benefits of a self-selected physical activity. S5.1.L1
Level 2: If the outcome was not achieved in Level 1, it should be a focus in Level 2. S5.1.L2
Challenge is a focus in Level 2
Level 2: Chooses an appropriate level of challenge to experience success and desire to participate in a self-selected physical activity.
Level 1: Selects and participates in physical activities or dance that meet the need for self-expression and enjoyment. S5.3.L1
Level 2: Identifies the uniqueness of creative dance as a means of self expression.
Level 1: Identifies the opportunity for social support in a self-selected physical activity or dance. S5.4.L1
Level 2: Evaluates the opportunity for social interaction and social support in a self-selected physical activity or dance.S5.4.L2
